provenance.reviewers: 4 read-only Plan subagents on Sonnet (correctness, security, tests, ticket-fit) + CI/SonarCloud

findings.title: A "+" in the last-name prefix is sent unencoded
findings.observation: claims Angular's HttpParams leaves "+" raw, so Spring reads it as a space.
findings.why: refuted — Angular 16 encodes "+" as %2B; this test pins %2B.

findings.title: Owner deleted between page and graph fetch fails the whole page
findings.observation: a concurrent delete makes the graph fetch miss an id and the request answers 500 instead of the remaining owners.
findings.why: design chose surfacing it over silent drops: openspec/changes/paginate-sort-owners/design.md:44

findings.title: Repeated sort=name&sort=asc is joined and accepted
findings.observation: Spring joins repeated values with a comma, so two params spell the valid token name,asc.
findings.why: means exactly name,asc; telling it apart needs raw-request parsing for nothing.

findings.title: Huge page numbers trigger a deep OFFSET scan
findings.observation: ?size=20&page=100000000 is valid and makes Postgres skip every row; a flood adds load.

findings.title: No test pins the V4 indexes
findings.observation: a dropped index or lost text_pattern_ops would leave every test green.
findings.why: refuted — DbSchemaExtractorTest regenerates DB.sql; CI drift check fails on a changed index.

findings.title: Latency-proxy test assertions compiled but never run
findings.observation: the new content/totalElements assertions were never executed against the proxy.
findings.why: deferred for budget by the plan: openspec/changes/paginate-sort-owners/tasks.md:15

findings.title: Ordering assertions depend on seed contents and collation
findings.observation: the ten hard-coded seed names and the 26+7 total assume today's seed and a collation.
findings.why: seed ids/rows are a documented test contract; first ten are ASCII, collation-neutral.

findings.title: OwnerTest.getAll lost its George Franklin assertion
findings.observation: it now checks only size 10 and the total, so wrong rows would pass there.
findings.why: OwnerListTest:89 pins the exact first page; the filter test still finds the fixture.

findings.title: Vanished-owner 500 path has no test
findings.why: needs a delete between two queries of one request; a mock-only test proves little.

findings.title: Task 4.4 not done: #25 not commented, Bizu not notified
findings.observation: the issue still claims the work was done earlier and lacks the breaking-change and Name/City-only notes.
findings.why: posting on GitHub awaits the human's approval; Bizu's handle is unknown.

findings.title: Type-mismatch handler changes errors on every REST endpoint
findings.observation: /api/owners/abc and any other bad-typed param now answer 400 instead of the generic 500.
findings.why: a malformed client value is a 400 everywhere; scoping it to one endpoint adds code.

findings.title: size documented without an enum of 5/10/20
findings.observation: sort lists its allowed values in OpenAPI, size only in its description, so generated types accept any int.
findings.why: springdoc emits integer allowableValues as strings; Spectral then fails the build with an error.

autofixes.title: Rejected query values echoed into the 400 body and the WARN log
autofixes.observation: ?page=<CRLF…> or a huge sort value was copied verbatim into ProblemDetail.detail and logged unneutralised, enabling log forging and reflecting attacker text.
autofixes.fix: name the parameter and the allowed values, never the rejected value; a test checks the body.

autofixes.title: Page-offset overflow boundary only tested at far extremes
autofixes.observation: only page=2147483647 and page=1000000 were probed; turning > into >= or dropping the long cast would stay green.
autofixes.fix: assert the last page whose offset fits an int is 200 and the next one is 400.

autofixes.title: A failed page hid the grid, so the user could not retry in place
autofixes.observation: on an error the table, sort headers and paginator vanished; the only way back was a new search, which loses the page.
autofixes.fix: keep table and paginator under the error banner; the paginator re-requests a page.

autofixes.title: Unpaged findByLastNameStartingWith overload left in the repository
autofixes.observation: only a test still used the List overload; it invites a future caller to load every owner again.
autofixes.fix: delete it; the test asks for a one-row page.

autofixes.title: Duplicated validation literals in the exception advice
autofixes.observation: the new type-mismatch handler made "Validation failed: {}" and "Validation Error" appear four times each.

autofixes.title: Generic length assertions and mutable injected fields in the grid
autofixes.observation: expect(x.length).toBe(n) reports worse than toHaveSize; router and ownerService are never reassigned.

assumptions.title: An OFFSET overflowing an int counts as an unrepresentable page: 400
assumptions.alternative: answer 200 with an empty page for any int page past the end
assumptions.why: the spec says unrepresentable pages are 400 and past-the-end pages are 200 — it never says where one ends. Hibernate fails on an offset over Integer.MAX_VALUE, so that is where I drew it; a human could equally read "unrepresentable" as "not an int".

assumptions.title: Sort tokens are strictly lowercase: name,ASC is a 400
assumptions.alternative: accept any case, as Spring's Direction.fromString does
assumptions.why: the spec lists exactly four accepted values and rejects everything else. Lenient case would be friendlier and nobody asked for strictness, which keeps this below 0.8.

assumptions.title: An empty sort= / size= / page= means "omitted", not malformed
assumptions.why: Spring's defaultValue applies to empty strings and the old lastName= already worked that way. The spec only defines omitted parameters, so empty is my call.

assumptions.title: The service sends only the parameters it is given; the grid always sends all four
assumptions.alternative: the service fills in defaults itself
assumptions.why: the defaults live on the server, so a bare getOwners() matches a bare GET. The grid sends its full state anyway, so the server defaults never decide what the screen shows.

assumptions.title: Add Owner is always shown, not only after the first load
assumptions.alternative: keep it gated on the first successful load, as before
assumptions.why: the spec wants Add Owner available across loading, empty and error. The old gate hid it on a failed load, so keeping it would contradict that.

assumptions.title: A non-empty total with an empty page shows an empty table plus paginator
assumptions.alternative: jump back to the last valid page automatically
assumptions.why: the spec only forbids claiming "no matches" and asks that navigation back stay available. An automatic jump would send a second request nobody triggered.

assumptions.title: V4 copied byte-for-byte from origin/db27oct, so the index name differs from the design
assumptions.alternative: my own V4 with comments and the name owners_last_name_pattern_idx
assumptions.why: a database that ran db27oct would otherwise fail Flyway checksum validation on boot. Whether db27oct was ever deployed is unknown to me, and this checkout's dev DB holds a third V4 that matches neither.

assumptions.title: Malformed typed params get a 400 on every REST endpoint
assumptions.alternative: validate page/size as strings inside the owner list only
assumptions.why: the global advice already owns REST error mapping per the style rules, and 400 is right for any bad client value. It does change the error code of /api/owners/abc from 500 to 400, which the spec calls an unchanged contract.

assumptions.title: Material's default "Items per page" label, not the sketch's "Rows per page"
assumptions.alternative: a MatPaginatorIntl provider relabelling it "Rows per page"
assumptions.why: the proposal calls its sketch illustrative, not final, so I avoided a custom provider. A product owner may still want the sketch's wording.

assumptions.title: End-to-end traversal checks the UI against the API's own order
assumptions.alternative: hard-code the seeded order of all 26 owners in the feature
assumptions.why: other specs leave owners behind in a shared DB, so a fixed list would break on reruns. The backend tests are the independent oracle for the order itself; the e2e test proves the UI pages through it without gaps.
